title: Sharing global constants across multiple files (using inline variables)
recap: C++17 inline constexpr variables let a header provide constants to many translation units. Each user sees the definition for constant-expression evaluation, while inline permits the repeated identical definitions and the linker treats them as one entity.

Grouping related constants in a namespace prevents collisions and makes their origin clear. Compared with extern const declarations backed by a source file, inline constexpr constants remain usable at compile time everywhere the header is included.
objectives: Define shared constants as inline constexpr variables in a header.
Group the constants in a descriptive namespace.
Use the constants in compile-time expressions in multiple translation units.
Avoid duplicated literal definitions and extern-only runtime constants.
warnings: A namespace-scope constexpr variable is not implicitly inline; write both keywords for shared header constants.
Changing a constants header requires recompiling every translation unit that includes it.
All definitions of an inline variable must be identical, so keep the single source text in one guarded header.
challenge: In time_constants.h, define inline constexpr minutesPerHour as 60 and hoursPerWorkday as 8 inside namespace timeConstants. Use minutesPerHour in main.cpp to calculate a 90-minute meeting at compile time, and use both constants in schedule.cpp to return a 480-minute workday.
hints: Place the namespace and both inline constexpr int definitions inside the header guard.
schedule.cpp should include the constants header and multiply hoursPerWorkday by minutesPerHour.
